intro:
Deesa is known across Gujarat for its potato farming, supplying a huge share of the state's produce, and it also houses a significant army cantonment that gives the town an unusually mixed character for its size. Weddings here draw both farming families and cantonment-linked households, and a full baraat entry, dhol and all, is a genuine highlight either way, drawing a proper crowd.

Plan My Baraat handles the whole entry for Deesa weddings as one booking: the double decker Baraat on Wheels truck, a dhol team, a vintage car or baggi for the groom's arrival, and the My Safa team turban-styling him and the full baraati group.
localArea:
Deesa sits in Banaskantha district, with roads that handle a fair amount of agricultural transport traffic, especially during harvest season, alongside regular town traffic near the cantonment area. We plan our truck's route with that seasonal traffic in mind whenever it overlaps with a wedding date on the calendar.

We cover Deesa and the surrounding villages regularly, many of which are deeply tied to the potato trade, and we're used to the practical realities of timing a baraat around a town where farm trucks and produce transport share the roads.
whatsIncluded:
Every package includes the DJ truck, sound system, and a DJ artist keeping the crowd engaged as the baraat moves through town. Raj Tilak comes with 2 dhol and chhatri lighting. Rajwada steps up to 4 dhol and adds a teddy or gorilla performer alongside the truck. Maharaja, the package most Deesa families choose, brings moving LED panels and lights up the groom's name for the arrival. Signature, our top package, adds a security team, timed pyro and confetti, and an upgraded American vintage car for the entrance.

The vintage car or baggi and the My Safa turban team are included in every package from Raj Tilak upward, so even the entry-level booking gives you a proper, complete arrival.
whyUs:
We're a Gujarat-based baraat planning team covering Banaskantha district regularly, and Deesa is one we know well, with crews comfortable navigating both agricultural transport traffic and the cantonment-adjacent parts of town throughout the year.

With one team handling the truck, dhol, car, and safa, you avoid coordinating four separate vendors yourself during a busy final week. We manage the timing so the truck's arrival, the dhol beat, and the groom's step out of the vintage car all land together at your Deesa venue.
pricingGuidance:
Pricing for a Deesa baraat depends on your package, dhol count, and any added effects like pyro or confetti. Raj Tilak is the most affordable way to get the complete core setup; Signature costs more because it's a genuinely bigger production, with more dhol, LED visuals, a security team, and the premium American vintage car included in the package.

Send us your date, your venue or area in Deesa, and a rough guest count, and we'll respond on WhatsApp with a real quote, usually within the hour, built around the specifics of your actual event.
planningNotes:
Wedding season runs November to February, which overlaps with parts of Deesa's harvest and produce transport season, so 2 to 3 weeks' notice in peak season is a sensible minimum to work with. Outside that window, a week's notice generally works fine for planning purposes.

A rough headcount for the baraati group helps us plan dhol positioning and how much room the truck needs, especially if your venue is near roads that see heavier agricultural traffic during harvest months.
closing: Message us on WhatsApp with your wedding date, your venue in Deesa, and an approximate baraati headcount, and we'll confirm the truck's availability along with a package recommendation, usually within the hour, tailored to your specific event.
